objectives.en: Count in sevens from seven to eighty-four without help.
objectives.yo: Kà ní seven seven láti seven dé eighty-four láìsí ìrànlọ́wọ́.
objectives.pcm: Count for seven seven from seven reach eighty-four without help.

objectives.en: Change weeks to days, because seven days make one week.
objectives.yo: Yí ọ̀sẹ̀ padà sí ọjọ́, nítorí ọjọ́ seven ni ó wà nínú ọ̀sẹ̀ kan.
objectives.pcm: Change weeks to days, because seven days make one week.

curriculum.objective: Apply knowledge of counting to local counting in groups of sevens (weeks and days), and change days to weeks
curriculum.note: NERDC teaches fives, sevens and sixties as one Primary 4 objective; this lesson takes the sevens.

say.en: A week has seven days. Mama marks every week on her calendar.
say.yo: Ọ̀sẹ̀ kan ní ọjọ́ méje. Mama ń sàmì sí ọ̀sẹ̀ kọ̀ọ̀kan lórí kàlẹ́ńdà rẹ̀.
say.pcm: One week get seven days. Mama dey mark every week for her calendar.

say.en: Today we change weeks into days.
say.yo: Lónìí a ó yí ọ̀sẹ̀ padà sí ọjọ́.
say.pcm: Today we go change weeks to days.

say.en: First, count in fives. Count from five to twenty-five.
say.yo: Àkọ́kọ́, ka márùn-ún márùn-ún. Ka láti márùn-ún dé mẹ́ẹ̀dọ́gbọ̀n.
say.pcm: First, count for five five. Count from five reach twenty-five.

say.en: One week is seven days. Two weeks is fourteen days. Three weeks is twenty-one days. Add seven each week.
say.yo: Ọ̀sẹ̀ kan jẹ́ ọjọ́ seven. Ọ̀sẹ̀ méjì jẹ́ ọjọ́ fourteen. Ọ̀sẹ̀ mẹ́ta jẹ́ ọjọ́ twenty-one. Fi seven kún un lọ́sẹ̀ kọ̀ọ̀kan.
say.pcm: One week na seven days. Two weeks na fourteen days. Three weeks na twenty-one days. Every week we dey add seven more: seven, fourteen, twenty-one, twenty-eight, thirty-five, forty-two.

say.en: Start together: seven, fourteen, twenty-one, twenty-eight. Say it with me.
say.yo: Jẹ́ ká bẹ̀rẹ̀ papọ̀: seven, fourteen, twenty-one, twenty-eight.
say.pcm: Make we start together: seven, fourteen, twenty-one, twenty-eight.

say.en: Let us try a smaller one. Two weeks. How many days?
say.yo: Jẹ́ ká gbìyànjú èyí tó kéré. Ọ̀sẹ̀ méjì. Ọjọ́ mélòó ni?
say.pcm: Make we try smaller one. Two weeks. How many days?

en: One week is seven days. What is seven and seven?
Seven, then seven more. Count on from seven.

say.en: Now you. Four weeks. How many days?
say.yo: Ìwọ náà báyìí. Ọ̀sẹ̀ mẹ́rin. Ọjọ́ mélòó ni?
say.pcm: Na your turn. Four weeks. How many days?

en: Each new week adds seven. Count week by week.
Start with one week: seven. Add seven for each new week.

say.en: Add seven for every week. Seven, fourteen, twenty-one. Then try again.
say.yo: Fi méje kún un lọ́sẹ̀ kọ̀ọ̀kan. Méje, mẹ́rìnlá. Tún gbìyànjú.
say.pcm: Add seven for every week. Seven, fourteen, twenty-one. Then try again.

say.en: Let us see what you remember. How many days are in six weeks?
say.yo: Jẹ́ ká wo ohun tí o rántí. Ọjọ́ mélòó ni ó wà ní ọ̀sẹ̀ mẹ́fà?
say.pcm: Make we see wetin you remember. How many days dey inside six weeks?

en: Each new week adds seven. Count week by week.
Start with one week: seven. Add seven for each new week.

say.en: Well done. Tomorrow we count in sevens once more. Soon we learn place value in four-digit numbers.
say.yo: O ṣe dáadáa. Lọ́la a ó tún ka ní seven seven. Láìpẹ́ a ó kọ́ place value ti nọ́ńbà digit four.
say.pcm: You do well. Tomorrow we go count for seven seven one more time. Soon we go talk the place value of every digit inside four-digit number.
